_comment: Hand-written, learner-friendly explanations and examples. Merged over WordNet by build_vocab.py. Each: {simple, examples[]}.

time.simple: Time is what we measure in seconds, minutes, hours and days. It can also mean one moment when something happens.
examples: I don't have time to talk today.
This is the first time I have been here.

people.simple: People means more than one person — human beings in general.
examples: A lot of people came to the party.
Some people like coffee, others like tea.

work.simple: Work is the job you do to earn money, or the effort you put into a task.
examples: She goes to work by bus.

water.simple: Water is the clear liquid we drink and that fills rivers and the sea.
examples: Can I have a glass of water?

house.simple: A house is a building where people live.
examples: They bought a big house near the park.
Come to my house for dinner.

world.simple: The world is the Earth and everyone and everything on it.
examples: She wants to travel around the world.
English is spoken all over the world.

school.simple: A school is a place where children go to learn.
examples: My son starts school next year.

family.simple: Your family is the people you are related to, like your parents, brothers and sisters.
examples: I love spending time with my family.

money.simple: Money is the coins and notes we use to buy things.
examples: How much money do you have?

friend.simple: A friend is a person you know well and like.
examples: I made new friends at work.

book.simple: A book is a set of pages with writing that you read. As a verb, to book means to arrange something in advance.
examples: I am reading a good book.
We booked a table for two.

light.simple: Light is what lets us see. As an adjective it can mean not heavy, or not dark.
examples: She wore a light blue dress.

run.simple: To run is to move fast on your feet. It can also mean to manage something, like a business.

play.simple: To play means to do something for fun, or to take part in a game or music.
examples: The children play in the garden.

happy.simple: Happy means you feel good and pleased.
examples: She was happy to see her friends.
They live in a big city.

small.simple: Small means little in size — the opposite of big.
examples: She kept it in a small box.

good.simple: Good means of high quality, or pleasant and enjoyable.

bad.simple: Bad means not good, or unpleasant.

hot.simple: Hot means having a high temperature — the opposite of cold.
examples: It is very hot in summer.

cold.simple: Cold means having a low temperature.
examples: Put on a coat, it's cold outside.

fast.simple: Fast means moving or happening at high speed.

slow.simple: Slow means not fast — moving or happening at low speed.

buy.simple: To buy means to get something by paying money for it.
examples: I want to buy a new phone.

sell.simple: To sell means to give something to someone for money.
examples: They sell fruit at the market.

love.simple: To love someone or something means to like it very much. Love is also that strong warm feeling.

help.simple: To help means to make something easier for someone.
examples: Can you help me with this?

learn.simple: To learn means to get new knowledge or a new skill.

teach.simple: To teach means to help someone learn something.
examples: My father taught me to swim.

read.simple: To read means to look at words and understand them.
examples: I read the news every morning.
He is reading a story to his son.

write.simple: To write means to put words on paper or a screen.

speak.simple: To speak means to say words and talk.

eat.simple: To eat means to put food in your mouth and swallow it.

drink.simple: To drink means to take liquid into your mouth and swallow it. A drink is also a liquid you can drink.
examples: I drink coffee in the morning.
Would you like a cold drink?

walk.simple: To walk means to move on your feet at a normal speed.
examples: I walk to work every day.

sleep.simple: To sleep means to rest with your eyes closed, like at night.

day.simple: A day is the 24 hours from one midnight to the next, or the time when it is light.
examples: We spent the whole day at the beach.

night.simple: Night is the dark part of the day, when the sun is down.

year.simple: A year is a period of 12 months.
examples: I was born in that year.

name.simple: Your name is what people call you.
examples: What is the name of this street?

place.simple: A place is an area or position where something is or happens.
examples: This is a nice place to eat.
Put it back in its place.

word.simple: A word is a single unit of language, like 'cat' or 'run'.

city.simple: A city is a large town where many people live and work.
examples: She moved to the city for work.

car.simple: A car is a road vehicle with four wheels for a few people.
examples: They drove to the coast in their car.

open.simple: To open means to move something so it is no longer closed. Open can also describe something not shut.
examples: The shop is open until nine.

close.simple: To close means to shut something. Close can also mean near.
examples: The station is close to my house.

man.simple: A man is an adult male person.
examples: The man in the blue coat is my uncle.

woman.simple: A woman is an adult female person.
examples: That woman is a famous doctor.
The woman smiled at the child.

child.simple: A child is a young human, a boy or a girl.
examples: Every child in the class got a book.

food.simple: Food is what people and animals eat to live.
examples: We bought some food for the trip.

room.simple: A room is a part of a building with its own walls and door.

door.simple: A door is the part you open to go into a room or building.
examples: Someone is knocking at the door.

window.simple: A window is the glass opening in a wall that lets in light.
examples: Open the window for some fresh air.
She looked out of the window.

table.simple: A table is a piece of furniture with a flat top and legs.

tree.simple: A tree is a tall plant with a trunk, branches and leaves.
examples: There is an apple tree in the garden.

dog.simple: A dog is a common animal that many people keep as a pet.
examples: My dog likes to run in the park.

cat.simple: A cat is a small animal with soft fur that people keep as a pet.
examples: The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

sun.simple: The sun is the bright star that gives us light and warmth in the day.
examples: Don't look straight at the sun.

rain.simple: Rain is water that falls from the clouds. To rain means this happens.
examples: Take an umbrella, it might rain.
The rain stopped in the afternoon.

road.simple: A road is a hard path that cars and people travel on.
examples: This road goes to the city.

shop.simple: A shop is a place where you buy things. To shop means to buy things.

job.simple: A job is the work you do to earn money.
examples: She has a new job at the bank.
Finding a job can take time.

doctor.simple: A doctor is a person whose job is to help sick people get better.
examples: The doctor gave me some medicine.

teacher.simple: A teacher is a person whose job is to help others learn.
examples: She wants to be a teacher.

student.simple: A student is a person who studies at a school or university.
examples: He is a student at Oxford.

phone.simple: A phone is a device you use to talk to people far away. To phone means to call someone.
examples: My phone is out of battery.

computer.simple: A computer is an electronic machine that stores information and does many tasks.
examples: I work on my computer all day.

music.simple: Music is the pleasant sound made by voices or instruments.
examples: They played music at the party.

game.simple: A game is an activity you play for fun, often with rules.
examples: The football game starts at eight.

story.simple: A story is a description of events, real or imaginary.
examples: Grandpa told us a funny story.
This book has a sad story.

picture.simple: A picture is a drawing, painting or photo of something.
examples: She drew a picture of her cat.
There are pictures on the wall.

color.simple: A color is what something looks like, such as red, blue or green.
examples: The sky is a beautiful color tonight.

number.simple: A number tells how many, like 1, 2 or 100.
examples: Pick a number from one to ten.

question.simple: A question is something you ask to get an answer.
examples: Can I ask you a question?

answer.simple: An answer is a reply to a question. To answer means to give that reply.

problem.simple: A problem is a difficult thing that you need to solve.
examples: We have a small problem with the car.

idea.simple: An idea is a thought or a plan in your mind.

life.simple: Life is the time you are alive and everything you do.
examples: Life in the city is busy.

health.simple: Health is how well your body and mind are.
examples: Exercise is good for your health.

body.simple: Your body is all of you — arms, legs, head and everything.

face.simple: Your face is the front of your head, with your eyes, nose and mouth.
examples: Wash your face in the morning.

heart.simple: The heart is the organ that pumps blood in your body. It also stands for love and feelings.
examples: The doctor listened to my heart.

voice.simple: Your voice is the sound you make when you speak or sing.
examples: She has a lovely singing voice.

language.simple: A language is a system of words that people use to talk and write.
examples: How many languages do you speak?

country.simple: A country is a land with its own people and government, like France or Japan.

war.simple: A war is a big fight between countries or groups.
examples: Many people want peace, not war.

peace.simple: Peace is a time with no war or fighting; a calm, quiet state.
examples: The two countries signed a peace treaty.
I love the peace of the countryside.

law.simple: A law is a rule made by the government that everyone must follow.
examples: It is against the law to steal.
The new law starts next year.

power.simple: Power is the ability to control things or do work; it can also mean electricity.
examples: The president has a lot of power.
The storm cut the power to our house.

group.simple: A group is a number of people or things together.
examples: A group of tourists took photos.

team.simple: A team is a group of people who work or play together.
examples: She works well in a team.

hand.simple: Your hand is the part of your body at the end of your arm, with fingers.
examples: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
He held the cup in his hand.

eye.simple: Your eyes are the parts of your face that you see with.

morning.simple: The morning is the early part of the day, before noon.

evening.simple: The evening is the part of the day between the afternoon and night.
examples: We watch a film in the evening.

important.simple: Important means something matters a lot.

beautiful.simple: Beautiful means very nice to look at or hear.
